title: Responsive web design
goal: Adapt a layout to its content and available width.
explanation: Start with a usable narrow layout. Use flexible widths, wrapping, and images that fit their containers. Add a breakpoint when content needs a different arrangement, rather than aiming at one phone model.
Media queries apply rules conditionally. In a mobile-first stylesheet, min-width commonly adds larger-screen layouts. A responsive navigation can wrap links before needing a collapsible menu.
Test at several widths, increased text size and keyboard navigation. A layout that fits at one width may still clip content at another. Include the viewport meta tag in the page head.
exercise: Build a single-column article and sidebar that becomes two columns on a wider screen.
hint: Use min-width to add the wider layout after the narrow default.

quiz.question: What should primarily guide a breakpoint?
options: The width where the content needs a layout change
quiz.explanation: Choose breakpoints by observing your content, then test a range of sizes.
